data.heading: Web Stack Battleground: SPAs vs Server Components
data.subtitle: The paradigm shift from Client-Side rendering back to the Server.
data.speakerNotes: Welcome to the thunderdome! Today we compare the legacy Single Page App against the new Server Component era.

data.heading: Core Lexicon
data.definition: The process of attaching React event listeners to a pre-rendered static HTML document, converting it into a fully interactive dynamic Single Page Application (SPA).
data.example: "Server Components dramatically reduce the amount of JavaScript needed for hydration, speeding up the Time To Interactive (TTI)."

data.heading: A Decade of Web Rendering Evolution

events.title: Server-Side Rendering (Classic)
events.description: PHP and Ruby dominated. Every click meant a full page reload.

events.title: The SPA Era (React/Vue)
events.description: Thick clients. The browser downloaded a massive JS bundle and built the DOM.

events.title: Static Site Generation (SSG)
events.description: Gatsby and Next.js pre-rendered HTML at build time for speed, but dynamic data was hard.

events.title: React Server Components
events.description: The best of both worlds. Rendering logic lives on the server, streaming UI to the client.

items.title: Server Actions
items.content: Asynchronous functions that execute on the server. They seamlessly integrate with standard HTML forms, providing progressive enhancement.

items.title: The 'use' Hook
items.content: Read promises directly in render, suspending until data is ready.

items.title: useOptimistic
items.content: Update the UI instantly while the server processes the mutation.

data.heading: Bundle Size Complexity (Big-O)
data.explanation: In traditional SPAs, the client-side JavaScript bundle size grows linearly O(N) as your application adds more components and dependencies. With Server Components, the client-side JS bundle remains near-constant O(1), as dependencies remain strictly on the server.

data.heading: Traditional SPA
items: Sends megabytes of JS to the user.
Waterfalls of API fetching on the client.
Poor initial load time (FCP) on slow devices.

data.heading: Server Components
items: Zero JS shipped to the client by default.
Direct access to databases and backend resources.
Instant initial load with streaming HTML.

data.heading: Form Handling Evolution

questions.question: What is the primary benefit of 'Streaming' with React Server Components?
options: It compresses images automatically on the server.
It allows the browser to render parts of the UI before the entire data request finishes.
It forces the client to download a real-time web socket connection.
It replaces the need for a database entirely.
questions.explanation: Streaming breaks the HTML into chunks. When wrapped in Suspense, the server sends the skeleton immediately, then streams the data-heavy parts as soon as the database query finishes, vastly improving perceived load times.

data.heading: The Modern Developer Stack Wrap-up
items: The pendulum has swung back from thick clients to smart servers.
React Server Components fundamentally change how we think about data fetching.
Performance is no longer an afterthought; it's built into the paradigm.
Meta-frameworks (Next, Remix, Astro) are essential for modern React development.
data.callToAction: Try migrating a small SPA to the App Router this weekend!
